History:

  • 21/10/2026 --- v1.0 -- Initial publication
  • 21/10/2026 --- v1.1 -- Updates with additional information

Summary

On 20 October 2026, the PHP project announced an upcoming security release addressing two critical vulnerabilities in PHP [1]. Public reports indicated that these vulnerabilities could lead to remote code execution [2,3].

The PHP team released the fixes today, 21 October 2026 at 13:30 UTC, in PHP versions 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35 [4]. Both vulnerabilities can allow unauthenticated remote code execution. Technical details are now being discussed publicly, and initial proofs of concept (PoCs) have begun to circulate. This raises the likelihood that attackers are already exploiting the vulnerabilities.

CERT-EU advises organisations to patch affected assets immediately. Where that is not feasible, organisations should consider isolating internet-facing applications from public networks until a fix is applied and verified.

Technical Details

The vulnerability CVE-2026-109618 (GHSA-w8hw-w9fx-j79w), with a CVSS score of 9.2, allows remote code execution through memory corruption during out-of-memory (OOM) handling [4,6]. PHP enforces its user-configurable memory_limit by using longjmp() to abort any request that exceeds the limit, which raises an OOM error. This can interrupt PHP while internal request data is only partially initialised, for example while parsing a form-based file upload. Request cleanup may then treat the invalid data as valid and try to free memory that was never initialised. That memory may still contain data from earlier allocations controlled by the attacker.

The vulnerability CVE-2026-109619 (GHSA-6wmf-4rv5-p3rp), with a CVSS score of 9.2, allows remote code execution through stale global state [4,7]. Internal state owned by a request can survive after its backing memory has been freed, for example after a fatal error. A later request handled by the same worker may use that stale state before normal initialisation resets it.

Every PHP installation that serves web requests is at risk, including PHP-FPM, Apache with mod_php, php-cgi, FrankenPHP and LiteSpeed. The PHP team considers mod_php the highest-risk setup. A demonstrated exploit shows that one unauthenticated request can trigger the attack before any application code runs [4].

Affected Products

  • PHP 8.5 versions prior to 8.5.12
  • PHP 8.4 versions prior to 8.4.27
  • PHP 8.3 versions prior to 8.3.36
  • PHP 8.2 versions prior to 8.2.35
  • End-of-life branches (PHP 8.1 and older), which no longer receive updates from the PHP project [4]

Many commercial and open-source products use PHP as a backend technology - these could be also affected, even if they do not directly expose a PHP installation. CERT-EU recommends consulting the NCSC-NL GitHub repository to identify third-party software that embeds PHP and may be impacted by these vulnerabilities [5].

Recommendations

CERT-EU strongly recommends updating all affected PHP installations as soon as possible to PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 or 8.2.35 [4].

  • Distribution packages: Linux distributions and LTS vendors received the patches in advance. Check with your vendor for updated packages.
  • End-of-life versions (PHP 8.1 and older): Some distributions and LTS vendors provide backported fixes, so contact your vendor or upgrade to a supported version. Because of the severity, the PHP security team has also published minimal source backports for PHP 7.4, 8.0 and 8.1 for organisations that build from source or have no LTS vendor.
  • rpms.remirepo.net users: This volunteer-maintained repository will not have updates on release day. The PHP team urges users to switch to distribution packages or build from source.

Where immediate patching is not feasible, organisations should consider isolating internet-facing resources from public networks until the fix is applied and verified.

Temporary Mitigations

Only an update fully fixes these vulnerabilities. The measures below reduce exposure to specific attack paths but do not make an installation safe [4].

CVE-2026-109618 (OOM corruption):

  • Set memory_limit=-1 in a way applications cannot override, such as php_admin_value in the FPM pool or Apache configuration. Check that no pool, directory or application setting puts a finite limit back. This removes the controllable memory limit failure, but an underlying allocation failure can still reach the vulnerable code path.
  • Set a low post_max_size: 8M for applications that do not need file uploads, 32M if uploads are required. Keep upload_max_filesize below post_max_size.
  • Consider enforcing limits at the web server or proxy level for decoded request size, input field count, multipart part count, header count and nesting depth. These limits must also cover requests without a usable Content-Length.
  • Use a container or cgroup memory limit as an availability boundary, preferably with a policy that kills only the affected worker. Do not use RLIMIT_AS or RLIMIT_DATA instead, because they can trigger the vulnerable allocation failure.

CVE-2026-109619 (stale global state):

  • Set session.upload_progress.enabled=0 and restart every worker. Apply this in php.ini, an FPM pool or a server configuration that takes effect before request parsing. Do not rely on ini_set() or FPM .user.ini. This blocks the confirmed session paths but not other variants.
  • On PHP 8.5, set fatal_error_backtraces=0 and restart every worker. This blocks the confirmed fatal backtrace path only.
  • Remove invalid or deprecated per-request settings that emit diagnostics before initialisation. Hiding diagnostics with error_reporting, display_errors or @ does not help.
  • Fix fatal errors and execution timeouts that attackers can reach, including failures in callbacks, upload or import processing, and cleanup.

[4] https://www.php.net/index.php#2026-10-20-1

[5] https://github.com/NCSC-NL/php2shell

[7] https://github.com/php/php-src/security/advisories/GHSA-6wmf-4rv5-p3rp

History:

  • 15/10/2026 --- v1.0 -- Initial publication

Summary

On 14 October 2026, Cisco published a security advisory addressing a critical vulnerability affecting the Advanced Malware Protection (AMP) feature of Cisco Secure Email Gateway. This vulnerability could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to write arbitrary files and execute commands with root privileges on the underlying operating system [1].

The Cisco PSIRT is aware of active exploitation of this vulnerability [1].

CERT-EU strongly recommends updating the Content Scanner Tools package or upgrading Cisco AsyncOS Software to a fixed release as soon as possible, prioritising appliances reachable from the internet. CERT-EU also recommends checking all affected appliances for indicators of compromise.

Technical Details

The vulnerability CVE-2026-76519, with a CVSS score of 9.8, is a relative path traversal flaw in the AMP feature of Cisco Secure Email Gateway that allows an unauthenticated, remote attacker to write arbitrary files on the underlying operating system. The vulnerability is due to improper handling of email attachments when the file reputation service is enabled. An attacker could exploit it by sending an email that contains a crafted attachment through an affected device, and a successful exploit could allow the attacker to write arbitrary files and execute commands with root privileges [1].

Cisco notes that Secure Email Gateway appliances can be part of clusters, and that private SSH keys used for authentication between cluster members could be accessed on a compromised appliance, which may allow the attacker to compromise other cluster members. Upon successful exploitation, attackers may also remove or hide evidence of exploitation and indicators of compromise [1].

Affected Products

The vulnerability affects Cisco Secure Email Gateway (both physical and virtual) running the following versions of Cisco AsyncOS Software [1]:

  • versions 15.5 before 15.5.5-014
  • versions 16.0
  • versions 16.5 before 16.5.0-780

The following conditions should also be met [1]:

  • The File Reputation service, which is part of Cisco AMP, is enabled and assigned to a mail policy.
  • The Content Scanner Tools version is earlier than 25.3.0.5525.

The information above reflects Cisco’s fixed release information. The fix is also distributed to all licensed and supported Cisco AsyncOS Software releases through an updated Content Scanner Tools package, and Content Scanner Tools versions 25.3.0.5525 and later contain the fix [1].

To determine whether the File Reputation service is enabled, administrators can choose Mail Policies > Incoming Mail Policies > Advanced Malware Protection or Mail Policies > Outgoing Mail Policies > Advanced Malware Protection in the web-based management interface, select a mail policy, and inspect the Enable File Reputation check box. To determine the running Content Scanner Tools version, Cisco provides the following CLI command [1]:

contentscannerstatus

Cisco has confirmed that this vulnerability does not affect Secure Email and Web Manager or Secure Web Appliance. For Cisco Secure Email Cloud Gateway customers, Cisco states that no action is required, as a fixed version of Content Scanner Tools is already deployed [1].

Additional information is available in the vendor’s advisory [1].

Recommendations

CERT-EU strongly recommends updating the Content Scanner Tools package or upgrading Cisco AsyncOS Software to a fixed release as soon as possible, prioritising appliances reachable from the internet. CERT-EU also recommends checking all affected appliances for indicators of compromise.

Compromise assessment

Cisco recommends reviewing the system logs for each affected device, with the following command, to identify exploitation attempts [1]:

grep "System Security" system_logs

One of the log messages in the following table may be in the output [1]:

Log messageRecommended action
System Security: Suspected compromise indicator was found. Contact TAC for further recommendations.A compromise is detected. Trigger the incident response plan.
System Security: Security scan did not complete. Contact TAC for further recommendations.A compromise is suspected. Trigger the incident response plan, and contact the Cisco Technical Assistance Center (TAC) for further support.
System Security: No compromise indicator was found.No compromise detected.

Vendor’s note: Upon successful exploitation of this vulnerability, attackers may obtain command execution with root privileges. With this level of access, attackers may remove or hide evidence of exploitation and indicators of compromise. Cisco strongly recommends cross-checking the network logs and the firewall logs outside of the impacted device to identify any potential suspicious activity, including but not limited to unexpected uploads that were initiated from the affected device to external IP addresses or downloads from malicious IP addresses.

In their advisory, Cisco does not mention any actual Indicator of Compromise. It is also not known how the log messages described above are generated.

References

[1] https://sec.cloudapps.cisco.com/security/center/content/CiscoSecurityAdvisory/cisco-sa-esa-afw-zqYJkjxp
